terminal_key: I put the key back on the desk. The desk doesn't want it back. Nobody wants anything back.
golden_token: I slap the token on the trading desk. 'Buy.' Nobody buys. Nobody's here.

LOOK.text: Three monitors, three charts, one colour: red. I look away. I'm working on that.

then.text: The drawer's empty. Thirty-eight pages of Terms for one key. Worth it. Barely.

else.text: Locked. The lock is a tiny screen: 'Accept the Terms to open'.

then.text: The drawer is empty. I already took the trading terminal key.

TALK.text: The trading bot on screen: 'Outperforming humans since 2024.' It's saying it to an empty room.

PICK.text: A smartphone, battery dead. The last notification says 'PRICE ALERT'. It always does.

then.text: The drawer is empty. I already took the trading terminal key.
I close the drawer. It doesn't ask me to accept anything this time. Growth.

else.text: Already closed. Closed and legally binding.

PUSH.text: I push the desk. The monitors wobble. I steady them like they're mine. They're not mine.

PULL.text: I pull open a side panel. Just cable management. Immaculate cable management.

GIVE.text: The desk doesn't need anything from me. It already got thirty-eight pages of my consent.

LOOK.text: Boxes labelled 'Moon Mission', 'Diamond Hands', 'Lambo Dreams'. All taped shut. Optimism, in storage.

USE.text: I peek inside one. Bubble wrap inside bubble wrap. Adrian protected everything. Except himself.

TALK.text: 'Anybody in there?' Bubble wrap pops somewhere. I'm choosing to hear 'no'.

PICK.text: A trading card in a sealed display case. Look, don't touch. The motto of this whole house.

OPEN.text: Inside: memorabilia, carefully labelled. Adrian was a collector, not a hoarder. Well... maybe both.

CLOSE.text: I close the box. Some dreams are better kept taped.

PUSH.text: I push the boxes. They're heavier than my bags. And my bags are heavy.

PULL.text: I pull a box off the stack. 'Moon Mission' falls and spills confetti. Nobody claps.

GIVE.text: Give away Adrian's boxes? Penny has an inventory. Of course Penny has an inventory.

_default: I hold it up to the mining rig. The fans spin faster. That's just the fans.
The rig has a lot of slots. None of them fits that.
I'm not feeding that to the mining rig. It eats electricity, not ideas.
terminal_key: I wave the terminal key at the rig. Wrong machine. The key wants a trading terminal, not a space heater.
keycard: No card reader on the rig. It doesn't care who I am. Most machines don't.
rainwater_can: The rig wants caffeine, not weather. Fernando wants weather.
empty_can: It already drank that one. It doesn't want the can. Nobody wants the can.

LOOK.text: A mining rig with more fans than I've ever had. It runs hot and judges quietly.

then.text: The rig recognizes my $ZERO balance! It shows me the secret TraitLab dashboard.
Same numbers. Same sticky note. 0301. The rig doesn't do small talk.

else.text: HOLDER: TraitLab Insider — the rig read your real wallet
A sysadmin note under the balance: the Ledger PIN is Gerald's birthday. 0301. Adrian's opsec is a sticky note with extra steps.
The computer runs TraitLab and the openPack program. Needs 1000 $ZERO for full access.

TALK.text: The GPUs hum in harmony. Low, steady, slightly smug.

PICK.text: A USB stick labelled 'STRATEGIES', soldered to the rig. Adrian's alpha, welded shut.

OPEN.text: I open the case. GPUs, fans, and dust bunnies the size of a rubber duck.

CLOSE.text: I close the case. The fans keep going. They don't need me.

PUSH.text: I push the power button. The rig reboots, sighs, and gets straight back to work. Unlike me.

PULL.text: I pull out a GPU. It's warm. I put it back before we get attached.

GIVE.text: I'm not giving away GPUs. Do you know what these cost during the shortage?

luxury_watch: I'm not putting the watch back in the armchair. It took me ages to fish it out.

LOOK.text: A massage armchair aimed at the monitors. There's a dent in it exactly my shape. Lots of people are this shape.

USE.text: I sit. Incredibly comfortable. I can see why Adrian never left. Except he did.

TALK.text: The chair purrs something. I didn't catch it. I'm sure it was nice.

then.text: Just empty springs and cushion fluff. The watch is already mine.

else.text: Something glints under the cushion — a luxury watch worth several ETH. It's tangled in the springs. I'd need something long and thin to fish it out.

OPEN.text: Hidden compartments in the armrests. Empty, except for one crumb. A historic crumb.

CLOSE.text: Closed. They click shut like they've got secrets. They don't. I checked.

PUSH.text: I push the armchair. It reclines automatically. Luxury is heavy.

PULL.text: I pull the lever. Full recline. Five more minutes. ...No. There's a case.

GIVE.text: I'm not giving the chair away. I'm not even sure I'm giving it back.

keycard: No reader on this hatch. It's just a hatch. I can push it like a normal person.

LOOK.text: A ceiling hatch with a pull-down ladder. It leads to the rooftop. Stars peek through the gap.

TALK.text: 'Anyone up there?' The wind answers. It's not helpful either.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a ceiling hatch. Gravity disagrees.

CLOSE.text: I close the hatch. The stars disappear.

PUSH.text: I push the hatch upward. It opens easily.

GIVE.text: The hatch doesn't want gifts. It wants to be climbed.

LOOK.text: An articulated desk lamp, the only light in this cave. The moths followed me in.

USE.text: I angle the lamp at the desk. Brighter charts. Not better charts.

TALK.text: 'Shine a light on this case, will you?' The lamp obliges. The case stays dark.

PICK.text: The lamp is bolted to the desk and still warm.

OPEN.text: I open the lampshade. A dead moth falls out. It died doing what it loved: chasing the light.

CLOSE.text: I fold the lamp down. The monitors glow green. Even in the dark, they're selling something.

PUSH.text: I push the lamp arm. It springs straight back. Stubborn. I like it.

PULL.text: I pull the lamp closer. My shadow fills the screens. I look like a real detective. Finally.

GIVE.text: The lamp doesn't want gifts. It just wants someone to change its bulb once in a while.

hotspots.keepAfterPick: La caja se queda con el resto de la pizza: solo te llevas una porción
hotspots.name: Pizza Box

LOOK.text: An open pizza box on the floor, fossilised.

then.text: One slice left. Forty percent cheese, sixty percent industrial lubricant.

else.text: Two slices. Forty percent cheese, sixty percent industrial lubricant.

USE.text: I consider eating the ancient pizza. My survival instincts win. Narrowly.

TALK.text: 'How long have you been here?' The pizza doesn't answer. It's transcended the concept of freshness.

then.text: One slice is plenty. I'm not opening a lubricant business.

else.text: The other slice stays. I think it's load-bearing.
I peel off a slice. It comes away with a sound like velcro.

OPEN.text: Already open. It's been open so long it's basically furniture.

CLOSE.text: I close the box. A small mercy for anyone else who enters this room.

PUSH.text: I push the box under the desk. Out of sight. Not out of smell.

PULL.text: I pull the box closer. The smell arrives first. It's been waiting.

GIVE.text: Nobody wants week-old pizza. Not even the rats. And rats eat literally anything.

LOOK.text: A half-empty energy drink. 'BULL RUN: 500mg Caffeine.' Adrian's blood type, apparently.

USE.text: I take a sip. Flat, warm, and now my heart is typing in caps.

TALK.text: 'Give me energy!' The can is silent. It already gave everything it had. Respect.

then.text: I already have a can. One dose of regret at a time.
Another can behind the monitor. Adrian bought these by the pallet.
I already grabbed the can. One dose of regret is enough.

else.text: I grab the can. Still some liquid sloshing around. 500mg of caffeine and whatever 'BULL RUN extract' is. Extremely hydrating, apparently.

OPEN.text: Already open. Adrian never waited for anything to settle.

CLOSE.text: You can't un-open a can. I checked. Twice.

PUSH.text: I push the can. It rolls under the desk, leaving a sticky trail of bad decisions.

PULL.text: I pull the can toward me. The last drops of BULL RUN slosh around sadly.

GIVE.text: Nobody wants half a can of BULL RUN. Not even the pizza.

hotspots.keepAfterPick: La bandeja se queda: el recibo iba entre los papeles (no dibujado aparte); el PICK de después lo dice («The tray is just sad printouts now»)
hotspots.name: Paper Tray

LOOK.text: A paper tray on the desk. There's a crumpled receipt sitting on top, half-buried under printouts of failed transactions.

USE.text: I shuffle the papers. 'Transaction Failed'. 'Transaction Failed'. A takeaway menu. 'Transaction Failed'.

TALK.text: The paper tray rustles in the draft. Even the paperwork is trying to escape this place.

then.text: I already grabbed the receipt. The tray is just sad printouts now.

else.text: I grab the receipt. One massive transfer, memo: 'PZ — care and feeding'. Somebody was paying for Patient Zero.

OPEN.text: It's an open tray. Nothing to open. It's very upfront about that.

CLOSE.text: Paper trays don't close. They just accumulate regret in paper form.

PUSH.text: I push the tray aside. Papers slide everywhere. I tidy them up. Penny would want that. I fear Penny.

PULL.text: I pull the tray closer. Adrian kept receipts. Literally. Hundreds of them.

GIVE.text: The paper tray has enough bad news. It doesn't need more from me.

hotspots.keepAfterPick: La caja ALPHA PACKS se queda y su LOOK lo dice («Empty now — I already took the ape costume»); el disfraz iba dentro
hotspots.name: Alpha Pack

then.text: An open backpack with 'ALPHA PACK' embroidered on it. Empty now — I already took the ape costume.

else.text: A sleek backpack tucked under the desk, labeled 'ALPHA PACK'. The zipper is half open. Something furry is poking out.

then.text: The pack is empty. All the alpha has been extracted.

else.text: I unzip the pack. Inside: a full ape costume — head, gloves, everything. A note reads: 'FOR EMERGENCY APE-IN ONLY. NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE.'
This must be what traders wear to 'ape in' anonymously. Genius. Unhinged. Both.

TALK.text: I whisper to the pack: 'What do you know?' The zipper rattles. No comment.

then.text: Already grabbed the costume. The empty pack can stay.

else.text: I pull out the ape costume. It's surprisingly well-made — realistic fur, expressive face, even little diamond-shaped buttons.
A tag inside reads: 'Property of the Liquidity Pool Recreation Committee. If found, ape in.'

then.text: Already emptied. Lint, a wrapper and the faint smell of ape.

else.text: I open the Alpha Pack. Inside: a complete ape costume! Fur, mask, the works. Someone left this here for emergencies.
The label says: 'Liquidity Pool Recreation Committee — For authorized aping only.'

CLOSE.text: I zip the pack shut. The alpha stays contained. For now.

PUSH.text: I nudge the pack with my foot. Something rattles. Something always rattles.

PULL.text: I drag the pack out from under the desk. Heavier than it looks. Like most of my decisions.

GIVE.text: Nobody here deserves this pack. Nobody's even here.

screen.speaker: Drawer
screen.text: TERMS AND CONDITIONS. Thirty-eight pages. Accept the Terms to open.

screen_again.speaker: Drawer
screen_again.text: Welcome back. You have unread Terms.

accept.speaker: Drawer
accept.text: By accepting you agree to give Adrian your left kidney.

accept_no.text: I'm attached to that kidney. Literally. The drawer stays shut.

read_1.speaker: Drawer
read_1.text: Page two. Adrian may change these Terms at any time. Including retroactively. Including now.

read_1_dex.text: Nobody reads these. That's the whole business model.

read_2.speaker: Drawer
read_2.text: Page seventeen. Section nine: Gerald is not a duck. Section ten: Gerald is a duck.

read_2_dex.text: My eyes are bleeding. Twenty-one pages to go.

read_3.speaker: Drawer
read_3.text: Page 38. Congratulations: you are the first person ever to read this. Drawer unlocked.

read_3_key.text: Inside: a trading terminal key. And a sticky note: 'PZ escaped via contract exploit. Check server logs.'

read_3_dex.text: Patience pays. I hate that it pays.

bye.text: I'll skim it later. Like everyone. Like always.

then.text: Founder mode is already active. The mining rig hums contentedly.

else.text: I insert the Golden ZERO Token into a slot on the mining rig. The screens flash: 'GOLDEN KEY ACCEPTED — FOUNDER MODE UNLOCKED.'
An admin panel appears. Adrian's full ecosystem dashboard.
Adrian built all of this... and then disappeared. Why?

script.text: I insert a floppy from the box into the trading desk's reader. The three monitors sync instantly.
The screens display: 'BACKUP TRADING STRATEGIES FOUND — FLOPPY ARCHIVE v1.0. Last modified: 3 AM, obviously.'
Strategy #1: 'Buy when mass is fearful.' Strategy #2: 'Sell when mass is greedy.' Strategy #3: 'Ignore strategies 1 and 2. Ape in. YOLO. NFA.'
The AI trading bot interrupts: 'These strategies predate me by two years and outperformed me by 340%. I am humbled. And slightly offended.'
At the bottom of the file: 'NOTE: If you own these floppies, you already understood the best strategy — collect the art, ignore the noise.' Smart.
ALPHA LEAK — Found Adrian's backup trading strategies

then.text: Just empty springs now. The watch is safely in my inventory.

else.text: I slide the antenna between the springs and hook the watch band. Careful... careful...
Got it! A luxury watch — heavy, gold, and still ticking. The back is engraved: 'TIME IN THE MARKET > TIMING THE MARKET.'
DIAMOND HANDS — Retrieved the luxury watch

script.text: I hold a floppy disc near the mining rig's USB port. Wait — floppy discs don't use USB. But the rig detects it anyway.
The GPUs whir louder. The screen displays: 'ADRIANLAB FLOPPY — GENESIS CONFIG DETECTED. Loading original mining parameters from 2024...'
The rig shows Adrian's first-ever mining config. Hash rate: pathetic. Power bill: astronomical. Conviction: immeasurable.
A GPU lights up with a hidden overclocking profile labeled 'FLOPPY_HODLER_BOOST'. The hash rate spikes. The rig hums a thank you.
The screen settles on a message: 'This rig mined the first block that powered AdrianLAB. Your floppies carry its DNA. Digital archaeology at its finest.'
GENESIS MINER — Activated the rig's original config

then.text: It's had one. Any more and it starts day-trading.

else.text: I pour the BULL RUN into the rig's coolant reservoir.
Its liquid cooling gurgles. I think it's been waiting for this.
Hash rate up three percent. I keep the empty can. Penny would make me recycle it.
